assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correcting spherical aberration turned the transmission electron microscope from an instrument limited by lens defects into one resolving atomic columns and enabling routine sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy. It is a clear, original invention (a discovery-or-invention case in the sense of the prize statutes) with transformative impact across physics, materials science and chemistry, including oxide interfaces, defects and 2D materials. I judge it from direct working experience with the technique.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theoretical design of the corrector, Haider led its realization and Urban led the first demonstrations on materials. The three credited names map cleanly to a fair trio. Other contributors such as Krivanek and Dellby (STEM correctors) are not among the credited names, so the instrument-family credit is not fully captured; I rely on my own knowledge for this.
assessment.maturity: Correctors have been commercial and ubiquitous for roughly two decades with abundant independent confirmation, and the recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: The TEM versus STEM corrector lineage means a case could be made for adding people who are not in the credited list.
Whether the committee regards an instrumentation advance as physics rather than methodology is a framing risk.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators opened a whole class of matter with protected boundary states, now central to condensed matter physics. The theory is original and the experimental realization in HgTe is decisive confirmation. Lasting impact is large and clear.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 classification and the quantum spin Hall state in graphene; Molenkamp led the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells. Theory plus experiment gives a coherent three-person configuration. Credit for the HgTe proposal (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) is not in the credited list, which leaves some allocation tension; I rely on memory here.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations, including ARPES on 3D topological insulators, and two decades of follow-up make this mature.
uncertainties: Competing priority claims for the HgTe proposal and the 3D generalization are not resolved by the supplied credit.
A compound discovery with 2D and 3D parts may need different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on the magic-wavelength idea, reach fractional uncertainties well below the cesium standard and set the path to redefining the second, with applications in geodesy and tests of fundamental physics. The idea is original and its impact is clear.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early clocks; Ye brought the systems to extreme accuracy and stability. Two names make a clean allocation, though other groups also contributed to the strontium and ytterbium platforms.
assessment.maturity: Multiple laboratories now confirm performance at the 10^-18 level. Recognition is timely, although formal redefinition of the second is still pending, which some may prefer to await.
uncertainties: Metrology achievements may overlap with earlier prize recognition of frequency combs and ion clocks, and the committee may regard the increment as incremental.
Ye also appears in other candidates such as the thorium clock, which could complicate combined recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane opened neutrino astronomy at the scale of a cubic kilometer. This is a discovery of clear importance, enabled by a bold instrument.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and Spiering was central to the pioneering detectors and the field's development. Large-collaboration discoveries make individual attribution delicate, and other founders of the field (for example in the AMANDA and Baikal efforts) are not credited here; this rests on my background knowledge.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed with several channels, while source identification remains at an early stage. The recognition is reasonable but source physics is still developing.
uncertainties: Fair credit to the collaboration and to earlier pioneers is unresolved with only two credited names.
The astrophysical origin of most events is not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, followed by the giant effect in MgO barriers, underlies read heads and nonvolatile memory. It combines clear physics of spin-dependent tunneling and interface structure with enormous technological impact. From a microscopy perspective, the coherent tunneling in epitaxial MgO depends directly on atomic-scale interface quality.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin and the Yuasa and Djayaprawira groups reported the large MgO effect in 2004. The credited trio is plausible but leaves out the MgO contributors Yuasa and Djayaprawira, and the Julliere precedent, so allocation is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and commercialized for years. The 2007 prize for giant magnetoresistance partly overlaps in subject, which could weigh on timing and novelty.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 prize (GMR) for spintronics.
Attribution between the 1995 discovery and the MgO enhancement splits the credit across different people.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recollision picture and quantum theory of high harmonic generation provide the conceptual basis of attosecond science. The model is simple, original and predictive, and it is the foundation for the work recognized in 2023, so it has lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Corkum and Schafer et al. proposed the semiclassical recollision process in 1993, and Lewenstein et al. provided the quantum theory in 1994. A trio from these papers is a natural allocation, though the committee may see this as theory underlying an already recognized field.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally verified for decades across many systems. Recognition may be seen as overlapping with the 2023 attosecond prize and so less urgent.
uncertainties: The 2023 prize may have already honored the field, reducing the case for a second award on the foundations.
Priority questions around the 1993 semiclassical papers are unclear to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene showed that twist angle tunes flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity, creating the moire quantum materials field. The discovery is original, rapid and highly influential, and it connects theory prediction to experiment.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group reported correlated insulating and superconducting states. Experimental credit is shared with collaborators such as Cao and Fatemi, who are not credited names, and a theory plus experiment trio is a reasonable allocation.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by multiple groups with a vast follow-up literature, but the field is still young and the interpretation of the superconductivity is not settled, which argues for some patience.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Reproducibility and sample dependence were an early concern, and I am uncertain how well settled they are.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED provides the architecture for coupling superconducting qubits to microwave resonators with strong coupling, dispersive readout and quantum control, and it is the basis of leading quantum processors. The idea is original and the impact is evident.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf and collaborators proposed the architecture and Wallraff and Schoelkopf realized strong coupling in 2004. A trio of Schoelkopf, Wallraff and Girvin is defensible, but excluding Blais, who is credited, and the qubit-development contributors makes allocation contested.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed. Superconducting quantum circuits have recently received recognition, and I am not certain how that affects the case for this adjacent topic.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior recognition of macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits is unclear to me.
A four-name credit list cannot all be honored under the three-laureate limit.
